sections.name: SceneErrorBoundary
sections.title: Fallback box for 3D startup failures
sections.what: Wraps the 3D view. Normally it shows its children unchanged. If the 3D renderer cannot start, it shows a warning box with suggestions, a Retry 3D view button, and a Back to start link when a home address is given. Any other kind of error is passed on so it is not mislabeled.
sections.why: The comment says failures and retries stay below the model loader, so saved data is never touched by a 3D failure.
sections.watch_out: Retry only clears the failed flag. If the browser still cannot start WebGL, the same warning returns straight away.

summary: A wrapper that surrounds the 3D scene so a crash inside it does not blank the whole page. It accepts an optional home link, which suggests the fallback offers a way back. The error catching logic is not in the visible part.
purpose: Protects the rest of the page when the 3D scene fails.
why: Likely reason: 3D graphics can fail on some devices, so the page should degrade rather than go blank. The reason is not fully visible in the lines shown.
how: Declares the two settings it accepts: the content to protect, and an optional link home. The code that catches errors and shows the fallback is not in the packet.
inputs: The child content to wrap and an optional home link address.
outputs: Either the wrapped content or a fallback view. The fallback is not visible.
risks: If the fallback logic is missing or wrong, a scene crash may still blank the page. This cannot be verified from the packet.
debug: If a crash blanks the page, check that the scene is wrapped by this component, then read the rest of the file for the fallback code.
